title: Why the Sky Is Blue
hook: Sunlight is white, yet the sky is blue and sunsets are red. The reason is that air scatters blue light far more than red — and the rest follows.
key_points: Air molecules scatter short-wavelength blue light much more than long-wavelength red.
This is Rayleigh scattering: scattering grows sharply as wavelength shrinks.
Scattered blue light reaches your eyes from all directions, so the sky looks blue.
At sunset light crosses more air, blue is scattered away, and reds dominate.
content_html: Sunlight arriving at the top of the atmosphere is essentially white — a mix of all colors. Yet look up at midday and the sky is blue, while the same Sun turns red at the horizon. The culprit is how air molecules interact with light: they scatter the shorter, bluer wavelengths far more strongly than the longer, redder ones.
extra_html: This effect is called Rayleigh scattering, and it ramps up steeply as wavelength shrinks. Because blue light gets bounced around in every direction by the air, you see it streaming toward you from all over the sky, which reads as an overall blue. At sunset the geometry changes: sunlight skims through a much thicker slab of atmosphere, so almost all the blue is scattered away before it reaches you, leaving the reds and oranges to come through. Wikipedia explains the scattering law and why wavelength matters so much.

related.title: The Electromagnetic Spectrum
related.hook: Radio, microwaves, the warmth of sunlight, the colors you see, and a hospital X-ray are all the same thing — electromagnetic waves, differing only in wavelength.

related.title: Reflection & Refraction
related.hook: A straw looks bent in a glass of water — not because the straw bends, but because light does when it changes speed.

flashcards.prompt: Why does the daytime sky look blue?
flashcards.back_html: Air scatters short-wavelength blue light much more than red (Rayleigh scattering), so scattered blue reaches your eyes from all over the sky.

flashcards.prompt: Which light does the atmosphere scatter most strongly?
flashcards.explanation_html: Rayleigh scattering increases sharply as wavelength gets shorter, so blue is scattered far more than red.

flashcards.prompt: Why do sunsets look red and orange?

choices.text: Light travels through more air, scattering the blue away and leaving reds
The Sun changes color as it sets
Clouds turn blue light into red light

flashcards.explanation_html: Near the horizon sunlight passes through a much longer path of atmosphere, so most of the blue is scattered out before it reaches you, leaving reds and oranges.
